# Objects

## `Array`

```python
class Array(MutableSequence[Any])
```

A PDF array; elements resolve and write as `Dictionary` values do.

### `Array.xref`

```python
Array.xref: int | None
```

The object number of an indirect object, `None` for a direct value or the trailer.

### `Array.generation`

```python
Array.generation: int | None
```

The generation number of an indirect object, `None` for a direct value or the trailer.

### `Array.is_indirect`

```python
Array.is_indirect: bool
```

Whether this is an indirect object rather than a direct value inside one.

### `Array.__len__`

```python
Array.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of entries or elements.

### `Array.__getitem__`

```python
Array.__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> Any
```

Return the resolved element at `index`, or a list for a slice.

### `Array.__setitem__`

```python
Array.__setitem__(index: int | slice, value: object)
```

Write `value` at `index`; slices are not supported.

### `Array.__delitem__`

```python

```

### `Array.insert`

## `Dictionary`

```python
class Dictionary(MutableMapping[str, Any])
```

A PDF dictionary keyed by name text without the slash.

Reading a key resolves references: an array, dictionary, or stream comes
back as a handle, and anything else as a plain value. Assigning a value
writes it at once, in one transaction. Plain values, lists, and mappings
are written as direct objects; an indirect handle from the same document
is written as a reference to it; and a direct handle is copied.

### `Dictionary.xref`

```python
Dictionary.xref: int | None
```

The object number of an indirect object, `None` for a direct value or the trailer.

### `Dictionary.generation`

```python
Dictionary.generation: int | None
```

The generation number of an indirect object, `None` for a direct value or the trailer.

### `Dictionary.is_indirect`

```python
Dictionary.is_indirect: bool
```

Whether this is an indirect object rather than a direct value inside one.

### `Dictionary.__len__`

```python
Dictionary.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of entries or elements.

### `Dictionary.__getitem__`

```python
Dictionary.__getitem__(key: str) -> Any
```

Return the resolved value of `key`.

### `Dictionary.__setitem__`

```python
Dictionary.__setitem__(key: str, value: object)
```

Write `value` under `key`.

### `Dictionary.__delitem__`

```python
Dictionary.__delitem__(key: str)
```

Remove `key`.

### `Dictionary.__iter__`

```python
Dictionary.__iter__() -> Iterator[str]
```

Iterate over the keys as `Name` values.

### `Dictionary.__contains__`

```python
Dictionary.__contains__(key: object) -> bool
```

Return whether `key` is present, without resolving its value.

## `Name`

```python
class Name(str)
Name(name: str)
```

A PDF name, such as `/Type`, held without its leading slash.

A name compares equal to the plain string of its text, so
`page.obj["Type"] == "Page"` holds. Writing needs the type, though: a
plain `str` value is written as a PDF text string, so write
`Name("Page")` for a name. Bytes that are not UTF-8 are kept as
surrogate escapes, so a name read from a file is written back unchanged.

## `Objects`

```python
class Objects(Mapping[int, Any])
Objects(document: Document)
```

The indirect objects of a document, keyed by object number.

Look up `doc.objects[xref]` to read an object, assign to replace it,
and call `add` or `add_stream` to create one. An object that
is an array, dictionary, or stream comes back as a handle; any other as
its value. Assigning a handle here copies what it addresses, so
`doc.objects[target] = doc.objects[source]` copies an object, whereas
assigning an indirect handle inside a container writes a reference.

### `Objects.__getitem__`

```python
Objects.__getitem__(xref: int) -> Any
```

Return the object stored under `xref`.

### `Objects.__setitem__`

```python
Objects.__setitem__(xref: int, value: object)
```

Replace the object stored under `xref`, which must exist, in one transaction.

### `Objects.__iter__`

```python
Objects.__iter__() -> Iterator[int]
```

Iterate over object numbers in ascending order.

### `Objects.__len__`

```python
Objects.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of object numbers in use.

### `Objects.__contains__`

```python
Objects.__contains__(xref: object) -> bool
```

Return whether an object is stored under `xref`.

### `Objects.add`

```python
Objects.add(value: object) -> int
```

Add `value` as a new indirect object, in one transaction, and return its object number.

### `Objects.add_stream`

```python
Objects.add_stream(
    data: bytes,
    /,
    dictionary: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    *,
    filter: Literal['FlateDecode'] | None = 'FlateDecode',
) -> int
```

Add a stream of decoded `data`, in one transaction, and return its object number.

`dictionary` supplies further stream entries; `/Length`,
`/Filter`, and `/DecodeParms` are set from the data and
`filter`, which compresses with `"FlateDecode"` or stores the
data as given with `None`.

## `Real`

```python
class Real(float)
Real(value: float | str | bytes | Decimal)
```

A PDF real: a `float` that keeps the digits it is written with.

A real read from a document is a `Real`, and so equal to, hashed as,
and computed with as its `float` value; arithmetic returns a plain
`float`. `lexeme` is the bytes that the real is written with,
when they are known, and travels with the value through copies, other
documents, and `pickle`. `Real("35.68123456789012345")` and
`Real(Decimal(...))` keep digits beyond a `float`'s precision;
`Real(1.5)` has no lexeme and is written in the shortest form that
reads back as its `float`. Assigning a `Real` writes its lexeme, a
`float` its shortest form, and a `Decimal` its exact digits.

### `Real.lexeme`

```python
Real.lexeme: bytes | None
```

The bytes that the real is written with, or `None` when only its `float` is known.

### `Real.to_decimal`

```python
Real.to_decimal() -> Decimal
```

Return the exact decimal that the real is written as.

## `Stream`

```python
class Stream(Dictionary)
```

A PDF stream: its dictionary, plus `read` and `write`.

### `Stream.xref`

```python
Stream.xref: int | None
```

The object number of an indirect object, `None` for a direct value or the trailer.

### `Stream.generation`

```python
Stream.generation: int | None
```

The generation number of an indirect object, `None` for a direct value or the trailer.

### `Stream.is_indirect`

```python
Stream.is_indirect: bool
```

Whether this is an indirect object rather than a direct value inside one.

### `Stream.__len__`

```python
Stream.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of entries or elements.

### `Stream.__getitem__`

```python
Stream.__getitem__(key: str) -> Any
```

Return the resolved value of `key`.

### `Stream.__setitem__`

```python
Stream.__setitem__(key: str, value: object)
```

Write `value` under `key`.

### `Stream.__delitem__`

```python
Stream.__delitem__(key: str)
```

Remove `key`.

### `Stream.__iter__`

```python
Stream.__iter__() -> Iterator[str]
```

Iterate over the keys as `Name` values.

### `Stream.__contains__`

```python
Stream.__contains__(key: object) -> bool
```

Return whether `key` is present, without resolving its value.

### `Stream.read`

```python
Stream.read(*, decode: bool = True, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> bytes
```

Return the stream data, decoded through its filters unless `decode` is false.

hayro-syntax decodes the filters, and a filter that it does not
decode, such as an image filter, raises `PdfError` instead of
returning encoded bytes. `max_size` bounds the result with
`LimitError` code `stream_data_size`, and the document's
limits bound the decoding; `None` lifts `max_size` for trusted
input.

### `Stream.write`

```python
Stream.write(data: bytes, /, *, filter: Literal['FlateDecode'] | None = 'FlateDecode')
```

Replace the stream data with `data`, given decoded, in one transaction.

`filter="FlateDecode"` compresses it; `None` stores it
uncompressed. Either way the previous `/Filter` and `/DecodeParms`
are removed and `/Length` is updated.

## `String`

```python
class String(bytes)
String(source: bytes | bytearray | memoryview | Iterable[int] = b'', /)
String(source: str, encoding: str, errors: str = 'strict')
```

A PDF string: its bytes, with `text` decoding a text string.

Write a `str` to store a text string (ASCII as is, anything else as
UTF-16BE), or `bytes` or a `String` to store the bytes exactly.

### `String.text`

```python
String.text: str
```

Decode the bytes as a PDF text string.

A UTF-16BE or UTF-8 byte-order mark selects that encoding; otherwise
the bytes are PDFDocEncoding (ISO 32000-2 section 7.9.2.2).
